questions.q: A SageMaker training job needs your dataset. What does the AWS documentation say about where the data must be?
options: On the data scientist's laptop, uploaded at job start
In the same AWS Region as the training job
In a bucket with public access enabled
In a Glue table, never directly in S3
questions.explain: The SageMaker AI docs state that your dataset must reside in the same AWS Region as the training job. Training data normally comes from S3, and public access is not required.

questions.q: Why put a version such as v1 in the processed data path?
options: S3 refuses to store objects without a version in the key
It makes Parquet files smaller
A new feature set will not silently replace the data an older model was trained on
It turns on S3 Versioning for the bucket automatically
questions.explain: A version in the prefix is a naming convention that keeps datasets separate. It has nothing to do with file size, and S3 Versioning is a separate bucket setting you must enable yourself.

questions.q: In the lesson's run, a 50,000-row table was saved as CSV and as Parquet. What was the result?
options: Parquet was about 31% of the CSV size
Parquet was about twice the CSV size
The two files were identical in size
Parquet could not be read column by column
questions.explain: The CSV was 2,080,741 bytes and the Parquet file 646,285 bytes, about 31 percent. Parquet is columnar, so you can also read a subset of columns.

questions.q: Which statement about S3 Versioning is correct?
options: It is enabled by default on every new bucket
Each stored version is a full object and is billed as one
Once enabled, a bucket can be switched back to unversioned
It stores only the differences between versions
questions.explain: Versioning is off by default. Each version is the entire object, not a diff, so you are charged for every version. After enabling, you can only suspend it, not return to the unversioned state.

questions.q: Which is the recommended way for a notebook to get permission to read S3?
options: Paste an access key and secret into the notebook
Make the bucket public so no credentials are needed
Email the keys to teammates for shared use
Use an IAM role attached to the environment
questions.explain: Credentials should come from an IAM role rather than being hard-coded. Public buckets and shared keys are security risks. Lesson 5 covers IAM for data science work.
